module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 313

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/313](https://www.erdosproblems.com/313)
- [A54377](https://oeis.org/A54377) (Primary pseudoperfect numbers)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos313

/--
This set contains all solutions `(m, P)` to the Erdős problem 313.
A solution is a pair where `m` is an integer `≥ 2` and `P` is a non-empty, finite set of
distinct prime numbers, such that the sum of the reciprocals of the primes in `P` equals `1 - 1/m`.
-/
def erdos313Solutions : Set (ℕ × Finset ℕ) :=
  {(m, P) | 2 ≤ m ∧ P.Nonempty ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) ∧ ∑ p ∈ P, (1 : ℚ) / p = 1 - 1 / m}

/--
Are there infinitely many pairs `(m, P)` where `m ≥ 2` is an integer
and `P` is a set of distinct primes such that the following equation holds:
$\sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} = 1 - \frac{1}{m}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313 : answer(sorry) ↔ erdos313Solutions.Infinite := by
  sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.solution_6_2_3 : (6, {2, 3}) ∈ erdos313Solutions := by
  norm_num [erdos313Solutions]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.solution_42_2_3_7 : (42, {2, 3, 7}) ∈ erdos313Solutions := by
  norm_num [erdos313Solutions]

/--
An integer `n` is a **primary pseudoperfect number** if it is the denominator `m` in a
solution `(m, P)` to the Erdős 313 problem.
-/
def IsPrimaryPseudoperfect (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ P, (n, P) ∈ erdos313Solutions

/--
It is conjectured that the set of primary pseudoperfect numbers is infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.primary_pseudoperfect_are_infinite :
    Set.Infinite {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n} := by
  sorry

/--
There are at least 8 primary pseudoperfect numbers. The first eight terms of
[A54377](https://oeis.org/A54377) are exhibited together with their explicit
prime decompositions.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.exists_at_least_eight_primary_pseudoperfect :
    8 ≤ (Set.encard {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n}) := by
  let S : Finset ℕ :=
    {2, 6, 42, 1806, 47058, 2214502422, 52495396602,
      8490421583559688410706771261086}
  have hS : (↑S : Set ℕ) ⊆ {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n} := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [S, Finset.coe_insert, Finset.coe_singleton, Set.mem_insert_iff,
      Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨{2}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 7}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 7, 43}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 23, 31}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 23, 31, 47059}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 17, 101, 149, 3109}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 23, 31, 47059, 2217342227, 1729101023519}, by
        refine ⟨by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro p hp
          fin_cases hp <;> native_decide
        · native_decide⟩
  calc (8 : ℕ∞)
      = ((S.card : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by decide
    _ = (↑S : Set ℕ).encard := (Set.encard_coe_eq_coe_finsetCard S).symm
    _ ≤ Set.encard {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n} := Set.encard_le_encard hS

end Erdos313

findings.description: The docstring says that the proof exhibits the “first eight terms” of A054377. Its witness set instead contains the seven smallest terms followed by 8490421583559688410706771261086. OEIS now lists 5998279018951962402 as the eighth term. The theorem’s lower bound and all eight displayed witnesses remain correct; only this description of the examples is stale. An independent Lean test verified that the newly listed number satisfies IsPrimaryPseudoperfect and is smaller than the proof’s largest witness.
findings.source_evidence: The current b-file https://oeis.org/A054377/b054377.txt gives “8 5998279018951962402”. The full OEIS entry, read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A054/A054377.seq, describes 8490421583559688410706771261086 as “previously in data” and still a term. Wang, arXiv:2605.21518, also supplies the new number’s prime factorization and verifies the defining equation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “The first eight terms of [A54377] are exhibited” with “Eight known terms of [A054377] are exhibited”. The theorem and proof need no change.

reformulations.difference: Lean existentially chooses a finite set of distinct primes satisfying the equation, rather than explicitly summing over all prime divisors of n as OEIS does.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The equation forces n = ∏ p ∈ P, p and hence P = n.primeFactors. Indeed, writing Q = ∏ p ∈ P, p and A = ∑ p ∈ P, Q/p, each prime p in P does not divide A, so A/Q has reduced denominator Q. The reduced denominator of 1 − 1/n is n for n ≥ 2. Conversely, the standard prime-divisor equation for n > 1 supplies P = n.primeFactors, which is nonempty and consists of primes. Independently proved the exact equivalence with the standard definition in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjectured theorems.

reformulations.difference: This variant asserts infinitude of the denominators n, whereas the Erdős equation formulation concerns infinitely many solution pairs (m, P).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Projection of the solution set onto its first coordinate has image exactly {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n}. It is injective because every solution satisfies P = m.primeFactors. Thus the solution pairs and primary pseudoperfect numbers are in bijection, and their infinitude statements are equivalent. Proved this equivalence independently in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A054/A054377.seq — full OEIS A054377 entry, including definition, examples, and updates

https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.21518 — Han Wang, Port Fillings for Primary Pseudoperfect Numbers: introduction, equivalence proposition, nine-prime-factor example, and scope of the conditional infinitude result
https://arxiv.org/e-print/1812.06566 — Jonathan Sondow and Kieren MacMillan, Primary Pseudoperfect Numbers, Arithmetic Progressions, and the Erdős–Moser Equation: Section 2 definition and Table 1
review.notes: All seven declarations were checked. Boundary tests exclude m = 0, m = 1, empty P, and nonprime entries; the nonemptiness condition is redundant given the equation and m ≥ 2. Direct computation verified all eight witnesses. Set.encard correctly handles both finite and infinite sets. The independent equivalence proofs and final tests compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/tests.lean. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/313 was blocked by Cloudflare; its equation was checked against Wang’s explicit reproduction and reduction, and open status against the problem database and literature. The full OEIS entry was read through its official data mirror.
